recipes.name: Grilled Tuna Steaks with Dill Sauce

steps.text: Combine lemon juice and 1/2 cup olive oil in a large resealable plastic bag; seal the bag and shake. Add tuna steaks; seal the bag and place into the refrigerator to marinate while the grill preheats.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Whisk together brown mustard, mustard powder, sugar, vinegar, and 1/3 cup olive oil in a medium bowl; stir in dill.

Remove tuna steaks from marinade and place on the preheated grill; discard marinade. Cook steaks until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 6 minutes per side. Drizzle steaks with mustard-dill sauce to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Tuna Steaks with Dill Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This sauce for grilled tuna is made with dill, mustard, sugar, vinegar, and olive oil for a bright, flavorful topping drizzled over fresh, hot fish.

review.reviewBody: The marinade is basic at best, and I recommend using one w/ some soy, and ginger added to the basic EVOO Lemon mixture. Now the dill sauce is simply amazing. 4 stars for the sauce alone.

I doubled the recipe, but found that doubling the sauce made on direction #3 does not need to be doubled, (I did double it) but would have been plenty without doubling.
Everything turned out perfect. I do not have a grill, so I used my oven and finished up with 5 min under the broiler. I nailed it! 
 ABSOLUTE PERFECTION!!!!

Skipped the mustard powder and used apple cider vinegar in place of white wine vinegar. Outstanding! This was the best sauce I have ever had on fish! In fact, this was the best fish meal I've ever made! The boyfriend was thrilled and ate it all and all the leftovers the next day. The sauce was great on the potatoes and couscous we ate with the tuna as well. Broiled my tuna for 6 minutes on each side, and it was still pink in the middle but o-so-tasty! Again and again, I will crave and cook this!

Marinade is simple and doesn't "flavor" the Tuna like some marinades can. The sauce is outstanding! Only two substitutions: I use red wine vinegar and I leave out the mustard powder. I season and sear the tuna filets, then serve them with the sauce drizzled over them and also some on the side.
I added stevia instead of sugar, and Sherry instead of white wine vinegar. And my wife wanted more than a drizzle. She even used the extra sauce on salad. It was great.

I cubed the tuna steaks, pan cooked them and served them over salad greens and cherry tomatoes with the dill sauce (as an appetizer for a dinner party). It was delicious and made a beautiful presentation! The dill sauce was more than enough for 6-8 servings!

This recipe was so unexpectedly great. I chose this one over others based on the reviews and I was not let down. I broiled the tuna, since I do not have access to a grill, and would suggest reducing cooking time. Other than that I wouldn't change a thing. I paired the tuna with boiled baby red potatoes and green beans, the dill sauce was a perfect compliment. I am using the left over sauce on a salmon fillet tomorrow evening. I have added this recipe to my stand by cookbook so that I can reference it at a moments notice. Thanks for the great new staple!

We really liked these, but I think I'd reduce the sugar to 1 TBLS if I made these again, as it was a bit sweet for our taste. I really enjoyed the dill/mustard, but the sugar was a bit much. THANKS for the recipe, SPLASHME!
Fantastic. I needed to use red wine vinegar for the dill sauce and it was delicious. We did have plenty of sauce left over, though. Any suggestions on the best way to save it?

this was awesome added about 4 tbs of graded ginger and 4 tbs of soy sauce to marinate. sause was great the way it was. even my 4 year old ate the whole thing had it with grilled asparagus and itillian squash
Do ourselves a favor... Reduce the sugar for 2 tuna steaks to 1 tbs. Too sweet. The mustard, dill and the substitution of apple cider vinegar were perfect
First go at grilled tuna steaks. Simple recipe. Family loved it. Served with some roasted asparagus, grilled veggies, some mashed red russets.
The sauce is very tasty and I think could also be used for salmon. Be very careful not to overcook the tuna. Tuna is best very pink in the middle so that it isn't tough.
I followed the recipe as is. Quick, simple and tasty. The brown mustard, dill sauce has a sweet and tangy taste. Recipe has been added to my favorites.
This will be five stars the next time I make it. The dill sauce is too sweet. I'll use half - maybe one third the amount of sugar. Like others, I added a little soy sauce and garlic to the marinade.
Just okay ......I like the soy/ginger/garlic flavor a lot more. Don't think I will use this recipe again.
I'm not a mustard fan, so I was pleasantly surprised with the flavor. Will definitely be making this again (and again, and again...)
The fish was yummy. I substituted stone ground mustard because my daughter doesn't eat spicy food. The sauce was a HUGE hit!! We will have this again!!
Real good and real easy too! The only thing I added was some fresh basil to go along with the dill. This sauce is also excellent on shrimp n pasta or just about any kind of seafood.

Made the recipe exactly as it's written... But only seared the tuna so it was extremely rare. Sauce was fantastic... Would love to use on other meats. Marinade did the job... Sauce was the star of the meal.
